🇲🇽🛢️ <u>DOS BOCAS NOW LEADS MEXICO'S REFINING SYSTEM</u>

The Olmeca refinery in Dos Bocas produced 27.1% of all fuel from Mexico's National Refining System in July — the single most productive refinery in the country, El Financiero reports. It processed 228,900 barrels, up 53.9% year-on-year and its second-highest total since startup, running at 67.4% of its 340,000-barrel capacity. The refinery AMLO was mocked for building is now supplying more than a quarter of the gasoline, diesel and jet fuel Mexico refines — the backbone of the energy self-sufficiency Sheinbaum defended this week.

🇲🇽📜 <u>ONE NATION, ONE LOYALTY</u>

The Senate has taken up Sheinbaum's constitutional reform to Articles 82, 116 and 122 requiring single nationality — no dual citizenship — of anyone aspiring to the presidency, a governorship, or the head of government of Mexico City. The stated aim: to bar conflicts of interest between those who wield public power and a foreign nation whose citizen they also are. A candidate holding a second passport would have to renounce it before registering. A country that spent two centuries under foreign pressure deciding that whoever governs it answers to Mexico alone. (El Soberano)
banner: REFORM: NO DUAL CITIZENSHIP TO GOVERN

text:
🇲🇽♀️ <u>WOMEN AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, WRITTEN INTO THE CONSTITUTION</u>

"Despite the misogyny of those who think women cannot govern, every day we prove the opposite," Mexico's first woman president said, reporting 1,001 LIBRE Centers for women and 27 million rights pamphlets distributed. Alongside it, the reform to Article 2 recognized Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples as subjects of public law: 25 billion pesos sent directly to 19,000 communities in two years, and 13,000 hectares of communal land restored to the Rarámuri, Yaqui, Seri and Wixárika peoples — with 177,632 more hectares in process, their fate decided by community assemblies.

🇲🇽💧 <u>WATER IS A RIGHT, NOT A COMMODITY</u>

After reforming the National Water Law, Mexico clawed back over 5 billion cubic meters of water from private concessions — enough to supply 90 million people for a year — and handed 12,346 concession titles to communities and small farmers, Sheinbaum reported. Cities like Mexicali and Tijuana that once paid private holders now hold direct public concessions. "We have spoken of what privatizing energy meant for the country," she said, "but turning water into a commodity had gravely serious effects." Some 24,000 water and drainage works are underway across 2,183 municipalities.
banner: MEXICO RECLAIMS 5 BILLION m³ OF WATER

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>"NO FOREIGN AGENT WILL BEND MEXICO"</u>

Closing her Second Informe, Sheinbaum drew the line: "Neither the corrupt of the past who want to return to power, nor those who would use the Transformation to protect personal interests, nor any foreign agent who wants to impose conditions on our nation, will bend the dignity of the people of Mexico." Her message to Washington and the opposition alike — here there are no divisions, no ruptures, only the defense of the Mexican people and their dignity.
banner: SHEINBAUM: NO FOREIGN AGENT BENDS MEXICO

text:
🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICO'S "LABOR SPRING"</u>

Under the 4T, Mexico's minimum wage has climbed 154% — from 2,800 to 9,282 pesos — while the average formal-sector wage hit a record 20,212 pesos a month, Sheinbaum reported in her Second Informe. Labor poverty is now at its lowest since 2005, with a 40-hour work week legislated for 2030 and app-platform workers folded into social security. For decades neoliberal orthodoxy swore higher wages would wreck the economy; Mexico raised them 154% and grew anyway.

🇲🇽📈 <u>THE SUPERPESO CLOSES ITS BEST MONTH SINCE APRIL</u>

The Mexican peso gained 1.87% in August — its strongest month since April — holding near 17 to the dollar, a level last seen in 2024, per El Economista. It caps roughly 5% appreciation on the year, defying every forecast of collapse under Trump's tariffs and anchoring the economic strength — record foreign investment, record exports — that Sheinbaum built her second Informe around.

🏳️‍⚧️🇲🇽 <u>JUSTICE FOR PAOLA: ARREST IN MEXICO'S FIRST RECOGNIZED TRANSFEMICIDE</u>

Ten years after Paola Buenrostro was murdered in Mexico City — the first killing formally recognized as a transfemicide — police arrested the suspect, Arturo "N," in the State of Mexico. Her death forced historic reform: the Ley Paola Buenrostro wrote transfemicide into CDMX's penal code, approved 47 votes to 3, and established mandatory protocols for cases involving LGBTTTIQ+ victims. A decade of impunity, now a name carried into law.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>210 TEXAS GUNS STOPPED BEFORE THEY COULD KILL IN MEXICO</u>

210 firearms — 195 long guns, 15 handguns, 93 magazines — trafficked from Texas were seized in Sabinas Hidalgo, Nuevo León, hidden in semi-trailer compartments on the Nuevo Laredo–Monterrey highway; 3 detained. Security chief Omar García Harfuch said the arms "will no longer reach criminal organizations nor be used to generate violence in Mexico" — part of 30,000+ US-origin weapons confiscated under Sheinbaum. The iron river flows one direction: south.
banner: 210 TEXAS GUNS SEIZED IN NUEVO LEON

🇲🇽📚 <u>MEXICO PUTS MENTAL HEALTH ON THE SCHOOL SCHEDULE</u>

Mexico's SEP is distributing 16 million free guides — 7.5M for students, 7.5M for families, 1M for teachers — and carving one weekly hour for socioemotional health into every secondary and high school. The "ABC of Emotions" strategy, presented by subsecretaria Tania Rodríguez Mora, is "preventive, community and territorial," backed by a 24/7 Línea de la Vida and 60 new community centers. Prevention as public policy — not a slogan.
